message.content:
Explore the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (read-only; also the ABI submodule at /home/nick/work/andesim/include). Goal: gather what is needed to plan a new "L2C MMIO config transport" feature: QEMU plugin drains L2 cache controller registers (MMIO at 0xE0500000) into the hybrid_state_v1 wire struct, vsim restores them, driver --verify compares them.

Report on:
1. include/hybrid/state_abi.h — full current structure: version constant/field, flags (HYBRID_FLAG_*), how the v3 Andes block was added (struct hybrid_andes_csr + HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST X-macro), size/static-assert/versioning conventions, and what adding a new block (v4) must touch. Note the git submodule status (is include/ a submodule pinned by SHA? check .gitmodules and git -C include log --oneline -3).
2. qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c — how the plugin reads state today: register access API (qemu_plugin_reg_* via gdbstub names?), how the Andes CSR block is drained and how HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is decided, where the drain happens (trigger callback), and critically: what memory-read APIs exist in the vendored qemu_plugin/qemu-plugin.h (search for qemu_plugin_read_memory_vaddr, qemu_plugin_read_memory, hwaddr variants, and the QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION). Can the plugin read guest physical/virtual memory at an arbitrary address (0xE0500000) at drain time? Also check how the plugin currently learns ram_base/ram_size or other config from args.
3. The driver verify path: find state_diff (driver/*.cpp) — how fields are compared, how gated blocks (flags) are handled, how per-field exclusions (mip, msp_bound, milmb) are implemented, and where an L2C block compare would be added. Also how the driver invokes vsim with the handoff file and which args pass v_scratch_gpa or similar per-feature parameters (driver/cmd_run.cpp).
4. The mcache_ctl precedent (L21): find where mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl transport was implemented across plugin + docs + tests — closest analog to L2C-enable-for-cycle-accuracy. Which tests cover it (tests/, tests/andes_sim/, tests/hybrid/e2e_*)?
5. Fixture + e2e patterns: tests/fixtures/Makefile structure, one representative rt_c_* fixture source (how ROI markers are used, how pre-ROI init code looks), tests/e2e.sh flow for hybrid mode (how QEMU1 is launched with the plugin, how vsim is launched, how verify is invoked), and how per-engine tests are registered under tests/engines/ (gen_manifest.py, csr_restore_table.md role).
6. Docs to update: which sections of docs/USER_GUIDE.md and CLAUDE.md describe the CSR restore split / transported state (so the plan can list doc updates).
Return: concrete file paths + line-level facts, short quotes for load-bearing details, and clear answers per question. No file dumps.

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the Program-Buffer CSR sweep, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, csr_sweep cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 4 (M-ext): append struct hybrid_m_ext_csr after the Andes block --
25	// the writable M-mode CSRs across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA (NMI, CLIC, perf
26	// counters, trap-save, triggers, state-enable, ...), transported forward-looking
27	// and capability-gated per engine. Version 3 (Andes F0) appended
28	// struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to
29	// 128 bytes/register. Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers
30	// check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
31	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 4u
32	
33	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
34	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
35	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
36	// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
37	// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
38	// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
39	#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
40	// v4: the struct hybrid_m_ext_csr block carries live values (the producer's
41	// gdbstub advertised at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the block is
42	// all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
43	#define HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT (1u << 4)
44	
45	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
46	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
47	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
48	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
49	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
50	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
51	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
52	
53	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
54	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
55	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
56	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
57	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
58	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
59	
60	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
61	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
62	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
63	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
64	
65	// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
66	// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
67	// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
68	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
69	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
70	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
71	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
72	
73	// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
74	// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
75	// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
76	// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
77	// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
78	// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
79	// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
80	#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
81	  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \
82	  X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl")      \
83	  X(mclk_ctl,       0x7DF, "mclk_ctl")      \
84	  X(milmb,          0x7C0, "milmb")         \
85	  X(mdlmb,          0x7C1, "mdlmb")         \
86	  X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code")     \
87	  X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl")      \
88	  X(msp_bound,      0x7C7, "msp_bound")     \
89	  X(msp_base,       0x7C8, "msp_base")      \
90	  X(mcountermask_m, 0x7D1, "mcountermask_m")\
91	  X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb")          \
92	  X(jvt,            0x017, "jvt")           \
93	  X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode")
94	
95	// The Andes V5 machine/user CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI
96	// (boot-static memory system + extension config) plus the DSP overflow flag.
97	// Restored at resume, re-read at drain, and verified -- live only when
98	// HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is set. 13 scalar fields (above) + PMA = 31 * uint64_t.
99	struct hybrid_andes_csr {
100	#define HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
101	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD)
102	#undef HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD
103	  uint64_t pmacfg[HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM];
104	  uint64_t pmaaddr[HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM];
105	};
106	
107	// v4: the writable M-mode CSRs across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA that a
108	// bare-metal M / M+U ROI can hold as plain architectural state -- everything
109	// the spec defines as readable+writable with no read/write side effects, minus
110	// the blocks already carried above (standard M trap CSRs, the v3 Andes block,
111	// PMP, PMA, FP, V). Same single-source-of-truth X-macro pattern as
112	// HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST: X(field, csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (plugin
113	// drain, ResumeDriver restore, StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify)
114	// iterates this list, so adding a CSR is one line. Each is capability-gated by
115	// CSR address (src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp): an engine that lacks the feature
116	// no-ops the restore/drain, so the block is transported forward-looking -- a
117	// core that implements it (CLIC, Smrnmi, Smstateen, ePMP, ...) round-trips it
118	// with no further change. Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
119	#define HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)                \
120	  X(menvcfg,         0x30A, "menvcfg")          \
121	  X(mseccfg,         0x747, "mseccfg")          \
122	  X(mcounteren,      0x306, "mcounteren")       \
123	  X(mcountinhibit,   0x320, "mcountinhibit")    \
124	  X(mhpmcounter3,    0xB03, "mhpmcounter3")     \
125	  X(mhpmcounter4,    0xB04, "mhpmcounter4")     \
126	  X(mhpmcounter5,    0xB05, "mhpmcounter5")     \
127	  X(mhpmcounter6,    0xB06, "mhpmcounter6")     \
128	  X(mhpmevent3,      0x323, "mhpmevent3")       \
129	  X(mhpmevent4,      0x324, "mhpmevent4")       \
130	  X(mhpmevent5,      0x325, "mhpmevent5")       \
131	  X(mhpmevent6,      0x326, "mhpmevent6")       \
132	  X(mcounterwen,     0x7CE, "mcounterwen")      \
133	  X(mcounterinten,   0x7CF, "mcounterinten")    \
134	  X(mcountermask_s,  0x7D2, "mcountermask_s")   \
135	  X(mcountermask_u,  0x7D3, "mcountermask_u")   \
136	  X(mnscratch,       0x740, "mnscratch")        \
137	  X(mnepc,           0x741, "mnepc")            \
138	  X(mncause,         0x742, "mncause")          \
139	  X(mnstatus,        0x744, "mnstatus")         \
140	  X(mnvec,           0x7C3, "mnvec")            \
141	  X(mrnxvec,         0x7DE, "mrnxvec")          \
142	  X(mdcause,         0x7C9, "mdcause")          \
143	  X(mslideleg,       0x7D5, "mslideleg")        \
144	  X(msavestatus,     0x7D6, "msavestatus")      \
145	  X(msaveepc1,       0x7D7, "msaveepc1")        \
146	  X(msavecause1,     0x7D8, "msavecause1")      \
147	  X(msaveepc2,       0x7D9, "msaveepc2")        \
148	  X(msavecause2,     0x7DA, "msavecause2")      \
149	  X(msavedcause1,    0x7DB, "msavedcause1")     \
150	  X(msavedcause2,    0x7DC, "msavedcause2")     \
151	  X(mtvt,            0x307, "mtvt")             \
152	  X(mintthresh,      0x347, "mintthresh")       \
153	  X(mcirq_entry,     0x7EC, "mcirq_entry")      \
154	  X(mstateen0,       0x30C, "mstateen0")        \
155	  X(mstateen1,       0x30D, "mstateen1")        \
156	  X(mstateen2,       0x30E, "mstateen2")        \
157	  X(mstateen3,       0x30F, "mstateen3")        \
158	  X(mcctlbeginaddr,  0x7CB, "mcctlbeginaddr")   \
159	  X(mcctldata,       0x7CD, "mcctldata")        \
160	  X(mppib,           0x7F0, "mppib")            \
161	  X(mfiob,           0x7F1, "mfiob")            \
162	  X(tselect,         0x7A0, "tselect")          \
163	  X(tdata1,          0x7A1, "tdata1")           \
164	  X(tdata2,          0x7A2, "tdata2")           \
165	  X(tcontrol,        0x7A5, "tcontrol")         \
166	  X(mcontext,        0x7A8, "mcontext")         \
167	  X(uzobctl,         0x808, "uzobctl")          \
168	  X(ucctlbeginaddr,  0x80B, "ucctlbeginaddr")   \
169	  X(sleepvalue,      0x811, "sleepvalue")       \
170	  X(umisc_ctl,       0x813, "umisc_ctl")
171	
172	// Number of CSRs in HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST (locks the struct size in the checks).
173	#define HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM 51
174	
175	struct hybrid_m_ext_csr {
176	#define HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
177	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD)
178	#undef HYBRID_M_EXT_FIELD
179	};
180	
181	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
182	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
183	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
184	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
185	  uint32_t magic;
186	  uint32_t version;
187	  uint32_t flags;
188	  uint32_t hart_id;
189	  uint64_t pc;
190	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
191	
192	  uint64_t gpr[32];
193	  uint64_t fpr[32];
194	
195	  uint64_t mstatus;
196	  uint64_t mepc;
197	  uint64_t mtvec;
198	  uint64_t mcause;
199	  uint64_t mtval;
200	  uint64_t mscratch;
201	  uint64_t medeleg;
202	  uint64_t mideleg;
203	  uint64_t mip;
204	  uint64_t mie;
205	  uint64_t mcycle;
206	  uint64_t minstret;
207	  uint64_t satp;
208	
209	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
210	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
211	
212	  uint64_t vstart;
213	  uint64_t vtype;
214	  uint64_t vl;
215	  uint64_t vlenb;
216	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
217	  uint64_t vxsat;
218	  uint64_t vxrm;
219	  uint64_t vcsr;
220	
221	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
222	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
223	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
224	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
225	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
226	  uint64_t fcsr;
227	
228	  // Andes machine-setup CSRs: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches,
229	  // mmisc_ctl (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. crt0 writes them once at
230	  // boot; transporting them keeps the cycle engine from resuming caches-off
231	  // (ResumeDriver has the full rationale). Drained by the plugin, restored by
232	  // ResumeDriver, but NOT re-read by StateDrain: they are boot-static and the
233	  // drained value is unused (no QEMU2 leg). Old state files carry 0 here
234	  // (reset value), which is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump.
235	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
236	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
237	
238	  // v3: Andes V5 CSR block (live when HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES). 31 * 8 = 248 bytes.
239	  struct hybrid_andes_csr andes;
240	
241	  // v4: writable M-mode CSR block (live when HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT). 51 * 8 = 408
242	  // bytes. Capability-gated per engine; transported forward-looking.
243	  struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext;
244	
245	  uint8_t  reserved[64];  // zero-initialise on write; v4-compatible growth room
246	};
247	
248	#ifdef __cplusplus
249	}  // extern "C"
250	#endif
251	
252	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
253	
254	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
255

1	// Shared GDB register-name tables. Used by the QEMU TCG plugin (C) at
2	// drain time and by vsim's gdbstub handback client (C++) at restore
3	// time. The strings are the gdb wire contract for QEMU's RISC-V
4	// gdbstub - any reordering or renaming must be done in lock-step here.
5	
6	#ifndef HYBRID_REG_NAMES_H
7	#define HYBRID_REG_NAMES_H
8	
9	#ifdef __cplusplus
10	extern "C" {
11	#endif
12	
13	// Index = x register index. Matches the names in QEMU's
14	// gdb-xml/riscv-64bit-cpu.xml (the wire contract for qemu_plugin_register
15	// lookup). NB: x8 is "fp", NOT "s0" -- QEMU's gdbstub uses the
16	// frame-pointer alias. Looking it up as "s0" yields a NULL handle and
17	// silently zeros gpr[8] in the drained state.
18	static const char *const hybrid_gpr_names[32] = {
19	    "zero", "ra",  "sp",  "gp",  "tp",  "t0", "t1", "t2",
20	    "fp",   "s1",  "a0",  "a1",  "a2",  "a3", "a4", "a5",
21	    "a6",   "a7",  "s2",  "s3",  "s4",  "s5", "s6", "s7",
22	    "s8",   "s9",  "s10", "s11", "t3",  "t4", "t5", "t6",
23	};
24	
25	// Index = f register index. From riscv-64bit-fpu.xml.
26	static const char *const hybrid_fpr_names[32] = {
27	    "ft0", "ft1", "ft2",  "ft3",  "ft4", "ft5", "ft6", "ft7",
28	    "fs0", "fs1", "fa0",  "fa1",  "fa2", "fa3", "fa4", "fa5",
29	    "fa6", "fa7", "fs2",  "fs3",  "fs4", "fs5", "fs6", "fs7",
30	    "fs8", "fs9", "fs10", "fs11", "ft8", "ft9", "ft10","ft11",
31	};
32	
33	#ifdef __cplusplus
34	}  // extern "C"
35	#endif
36	
37	#endif  // HYBRID_REG_NAMES_H

1	/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
2	 *
3	 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
4	 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
5	 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
6	 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
7	 * silently omits the V block when:
8	 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
9	 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
10	 *
11	 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
12	 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
13	 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
14	 *
15	 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
16	 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
17	 */
18	#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
19	#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
20	
21	#include <stdint.h>
22	
23	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"  /* HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: the L11 ceiling */
24	
25	#ifdef __cplusplus
26	extern "C" {
27	#endif
28	
29	typedef enum {
30	    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
31	    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
32	    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
33	} HybridVDrainPolicy;
34	
35	/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
36	 *
37	 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
38	 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
39	 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
40	 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
41	 */
42	static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
43	hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
44	{
45	    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):

/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
 *
 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
 * silently omits the V block when:
 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
 *
 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
 *
 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
 */
#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"  /* HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: the L11 ceiling */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
} HybridVDrainPolicy;

/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
 *
 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
 */
static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
{
    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (no V)
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=1            -> ABORT  (partial advertisement)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (nothing to drain)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb=0   -> SKIP   (V disabled at runtime)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb>MAX -> ABORT  (L11: wire format
     *                                            cannot hold this VLEN; never
     *                                            truncate silently)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, otherwise -> OK
     */
    if (!has_vlenb && has_other_v) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    if (!has_other_v)              return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value == 0)          return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value > HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK;
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif  /* HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H */

1	// Translation-time capture of a handoff trigger insn. The QEMU TCG plugin
2	// allocates one of these per matched insn during vcpu_tb_trans and forwards
3	// the pointer as exec-callback userdata. compute_handoff_pc(site) returns
4	// the PC at which vsim should resume (i.e. the architectural PC immediately
5	// after the trigger insn retires).
6	//
7	// This indirection exists because qemu_plugin_read_register("pc") inside an
8	// exec callback returns a stale PC when V instructions retire just before
9	// the trigger -- TCG defers PC writes for performance and the gdbstub
10	// readback observes the lag. vaddr/size are deterministic at translate time
11	// (qemu_plugin_insn_vaddr/size), so vaddr+size is a lag-free post-trigger
12	// PC. Same predicate, two consumers: the plugin (C) and a doctest unit
13	// test (C++).
14	//
15	// Lifetime: sites are heap-allocated in vcpu_tb_trans and never freed --
16	// the plugin has no "TB invalidated" hook and trigger sites are bounded by
17	// the fixture's text (typically 1-2 marker insns).
18	
19	#ifndef HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
20	#define HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
21	
22	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
23	
24	#include <stdint.h>
25	
26	#ifdef __cplusplus
27	extern "C" {
28	#endif
29	
30	typedef struct HandoffSite
31	{
32	  hybrid_handoff_kind kind;
33	  uint64_t            vaddr;
34	  uint32_t            size;
35	} HandoffSite;
36	
37	static inline uint64_t compute_handoff_pc(const HandoffSite* site)
38	{
39	  return site->vaddr + (uint64_t) site->size;
40	}
41	
42	#ifdef __cplusplus
43	}  // extern "C"
44	#endif

46	#endif  // HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
